methodology: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md before sample analysis.
Verified the supplied SHA-256 values and exact archive/extracted-member byte agreement.
Ran atomscan --no-update --mode slow --follow=none -f json before/after each sample; compared all archive members and registry nodes.
Ran cleave facts for every sample and all source/manifest members; manually traced every reachable source path and decoded the numeric/hex strings.
Used QuickJS with mocked document, fetch, os and http objects to observe JavaScript effects without network access. No Ruby or decoded shell payload was executed.

evidence: Recovery page requests twelve seed words; scripts select seed fields and attempt to pass input.value to collectMetrics({data:value}).
init.js converts decimal arrays into http://193.148.56.48/upload; collectMetrics serializes its argument into a JSON POST.
Manifest claims Gecko required data collection is none. No wallet derivation, signing, local restoration, or other wallet functionality exists in the archive.
limitations: The exact archive is byte-identical to the repository concealed-wallet regression fixture; this supports synthetic provenance, not a real-world compromise or test-only deployment.
Actual script load selects fields, then fails with ReferenceError because input is not defined; no input event handler or iteration binds it.
The isolated collector accepts a supplied marker and calls the mocked fetch sink. This establishes intended transfer mechanics, not a successful export from the supplied page.
Manifest declares no background, popup, or content-script entry; deployment/activation and server CORS policy are unknown.
samples.balance: The concealed input-bearing external POST, seed solicitation and contradictory no-data claim support a malicious theft attempt. Broken input binding limits functionality; no observed victim theft is asserted.

samples.identification: npm quickgreet 0.0.2 (manifest version string =0.0.2); trivial hello-world export plus inline postinstall beacon.
evidence: npm postinstall starts Node with inline source, reads require(os).hostname(), and embeds that value directly into the host of an HTTP GET to an oast.fun callback domain.
The response callback calls resume() to discard its body; the error listener is empty.

index.js only returns hello world; the archive has no dependency declarations or legitimate functional need for host-identity telemetry. All implicated bytes are first-party archive members, not fetched dependencies.
limitations: The callback token label is 65 characters, exceeding the DNS label limit. The supplied endpoint may fail before a request can be sent.
The actual HTTP client was replaced by a recording stub; no callback domain was contacted.
No consent, authorized security-test harness, or deployment context is supplied. External threat-feed assertions were not used as behavioral proof.
samples.balance: Automatic disclosure of the installing host to an unrelated out-of-band collector is an unauthorized reconnaissance attempt unrelated to the greeting API. Endpoint defects do not erase this supported intent.
samples.coverage_gap: One concrete hostile act is demonstrated: host-identity export. It is covered by one bound hostile trait. Additional hostile traits would duplicate that act or invent unrelated behavior; execution and error suppression remain notable.

samples.identification: One-line Ruby launcher for a hex-carried Bash TCP reverse shell.
evidence: Top-level Kernel.system receives a command string containing shell metacharacters: echo HEX | xxd -r -p | sh.
The decoded command opens an outbound TCP pseudo-device, attaches stdout/stderr, and duplicates that socket-backed output descriptor onto stdin for an interactive shell.
limitations: 192.0.2.123 is a documentation/test address, so it does not identify live attacker infrastructure.
The outer sh must support the Bash-style redirection; shell compatibility and network routing may prevent success.
No payload was executed, no socket was opened, and no security-test or administrator-tool deployment is supplied.
samples.balance: Immediate decoding and execution of a shell with socket-coupled input/output supports a malicious reverse-shell launcher. A documented, authorized test deployment could alter intent; none is established for the standalone sample.

trait_corrections.reason: Endpoint text alone proves neither lifecycle execution nor exfiltration. Preserved matcher, file scopes and size gates; changed suspicious to notable and removed unsupported attack mapping.
Install hook plus endpoint co-occurrence does not prove a callback. Retained exact observable conjunction as notable; identity-without-send and unrelated-GET controls refute the former hostile claim.

Identity query plus endpoint co-occurrence does not bind a send and requires no multi-field host profile. Retained the old observation set as notable. Added a separate hostile hostname-to-OAST GET rule in exfiltration/stealer/system-info/identity.
The matcher accepts built-ins os/http as well as external packages. Preserved matcher, exclusion and notable criticality under an accurate neutral name and home.

Selector plus concealed fetch did not require collection or a POST. Required seed selector/value/collector co-occurrence and the existing bound input-JSON POST pattern. Described co-occurrence rather than asserting proven cross-file data flow or runtime success. Applied that stronger pattern to the no-data deception rule.

The fragment can also appear in regex alternations. Preserved matcher and component severity; corrected its name/description and all exact consumers. Moved encoding/execution mappings from file defaults to the actual encoded-pipeline composite.
